“This could be a referendum on President Trump. It could be the referendum on Congress or the Republican Party,” she told The Associated Press on Thursday as she sat in a U-Haul. “I think it’s all of it.”

“We had solutions and we didn’t take action,” she said.

And despite the Democratic Party’s astonishing wins across the board earlier this month, Boebert won’t abandon Trump.

“I’m not mad at the president,” she said, conceding that “the president did some things that hurt my voters.”

She also wouldn’t denounce her MAGA label.

“When Jesus comes back and I’m raptured up, like all these labels are just going to fly off anyway,” she told the publication. “I respect President Trump, I still work with him, I want to continue to work with him. Not for him, with him.”

Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) was more blunt in his criticism of Trump during a memorable interview with CNN last week.

“The economy belongs to President Trump. He might not have fathered this child, but he’s gotta raise it,” Kennedy said.

The Louisiana Republican also said Vance’s assessment that Republicans lost because of the war in Iran was incorrect.

“This loss was not because of Iran. That might have played a part, but I don’t think every statewide Republican in Texas lost their election — every single one — because they think American foreign policy is too interventionist. I mean, put down the crack pipe. It’s a lot deeper than that,” Kennedy shared.
